home.learnText: Play with Clef and learn music and code, step by step.
home.composeText: Make anything you like with every block. No lessons.

map.title: Pick a lesson
map.locked: Finish the lesson before this one to open it

studio.codeEmpty: Put a block inside My song to see its code here.
studio.codeExplain: This is real Strudel code. Your blocks wrote it!
studio.staffEmpty: Put a beat or a melody inside My song to see it written as music.
studio.staffExplain: This is your song written on a staff, the way musicians read music.
studio.drumKey: On a drum staff, each sound has its own line or space.
studio.emptySong: Put a block inside My song first!
studio.error: Hmm, that didn't work. Try changing a block.

tooltips.song: Everything inside My song plays when you press Play.
tooltips.sound: Plays one sound, once every bar. Code: s("bd")
tooltips.beat4: Four steps. Tap a square to turn it on or off. Code: s("bd ~ bd ~")
tooltips.beat8: Eight quick steps. Code: s("hh hh hh hh hh hh hh hh")
tooltips.melody: Put notes inside to play a tune. Pick normal, bouncy or smooth. Code: note("c4 e4 g4")
tooltips.note: One note. Pick how high it is and how long it lasts.
tooltips.speed: Put tracks inside to play them twice as fast, or half as fast. Code: .fast(2) or .slow(2)
tooltips.scale: A tune made of steps on a scale ladder. Code: n("0 2 4").scale("C4:major")
tooltips.step: One step of the scale ladder. Step 1 is the bottom, step 8 is the top.
tooltips.chords: Four chords, two beats each. Code: note("[c4,e4,g4] ...")

clef.hello: Hi {name}! I'm Clef. Let's make music!
clef.helloNoName: Hi! I'm Clef. Let's make music!
clef.lessonDone: You finished the lesson! You earned a star!
clef.compose: Make anything you like! Press Play to hear it.

listen.say: Let's listen first! Press the big ear button.

drag.say: Find the pink play block. Drag it inside My song.
drag.hint: The pink block is on the left. Drop it just under My song, so it clicks in.

play.say: Now press the green Play button at the top!
play.hint: The Play button is green with a triangle.

change.say: Tap the little arrow on your block and pick a different sound. Try the sheep!
change.hint: Tap the word kick on your block. A list of sounds pops up.

card.musicText: Every instrument makes its own special sound. A drum sounds different to a sheep!
card.codeText: s() is a function: an instruction that does a job. This one plays a sound.

listen.say: This is a beat. Clap along with it! Press the ear button.

drag.say: Drag the purple beat block, the one with squares, inside My song.
drag.hint: It's the purple block with four squares.

fill.say: Tap all four squares to turn them on.
fill.hint: Tap each grey square once. It turns white when it's on.

play.say: Press Play. Can you hear four kicks? That's the beat!

code.say: Look at the code. Each kick is written as b d. Four kicks, one after another. That's called a sequence!
code.hint: The code is on the right side.

card.musicText: The beat is the steady pulse you can clap or march along to.
card.codeText: "bd bd bd bd" is a sequence: steps that happen one after another.

listen.say: Listen. Some steps are quiet! A quiet step is called a rest.

drag.say: Drag a beat block inside My song.

pattern.say: Turn on only the first and the third squares.
pattern.hint: On, off, on, off. Tap a white square to turn it off.

play.say: Press Play. Boom, rest, boom, rest. Can you hear the gaps?

code.say: In the code, a rest is a squiggle. Can you find the squiggles?
code.hint: They are glowing yellow in the code.

own.say: Now make your own rhythm! Leave at least one square off.
own.hint: Tap squares on and off until you like how it sounds.

card.musicText: A rest is a moment of silence. Sounds and rests together make a rhythm.
card.codeText: ~ is a symbol. In Strudel it means: be quiet for one step.

listen.say: This is a rock beat. Three instruments are playing at the same time!

kick.say: Put a beat block inside My song. Make it kick on squares one and three.
kick.hint: Pick the drum, then turn on the first and third squares.

snare.say: Add another beat block underneath. Pick the snare, and turn on squares two and four.
snare.hint: Tap kick on the new block and choose snare.

hats.say: Now add the long blue beat block. Pick the hi-hat, and turn on all eight squares.
hats.hint: The blue block has eight squares. The hi-hat has a top hat.

play.say: Press Play. You made a rock beat!

code.say: See the word stack in the code? Stack means: play these together.
code.hint: Stack is glowing at the top of the code.

card.musicText: When instruments play at the same time, the music sounds bigger and fuller.
card.codeText: stack() plays patterns side by side, all at once. Programmers call this running in parallel.

listen.say: Listen. The same beat plays at normal speed, then twice as fast!

beat.say: Put a beat block in My song. Turn on all four squares.
beat.hint: The purple block with squares. Tap every square.

wrap.say: Find the orange rabbit block. Drag it into My song, and put your beat inside it.
wrap.hint: Drag the rabbit block in first, then drag your beat into the rabbit's mouth.

play.say: Press Play. Zoom! Everything is twice as fast.

slow.say: Now tap the rabbit and pick the turtle. Slow and sleepy!
slow.hint: Tap the words faster times two, then choose the turtle.

code.say: Look at the code. fast and slow have a number in brackets. That number is called a parameter. It tells the function how much.
code.hint: The glowing words at the end of the code.

card.musicText: Tempo is how fast music goes. Twice as fast makes every sound twice as short.
card.codeText: In .fast(2), the 2 is a parameter: a number you give a function to change what it does.

listen.say: Listen. Low C, then high C. Same note name, but one is higher!

melody.say: Drag the green melody block into My song.
melody.hint: The green block with a gap inside.

lowhigh.say: Put in a red low C, and the dark red high C.
lowhigh.hint: There are two red C notes. The second red one at the bottom is the high C.

play.say: Press Play. Low, high, low, high!

code.say: In the code, c4 and c5 are both C. The number tells how high. Five is higher than four!
code.hint: c4 and c5 are glowing in the code.

climb.say: Now make a tune with four notes that climbs up, higher and higher!
climb.hint: Each note must be higher than the one before. Try C, E, G, high C.

card.musicText: Pitch is how high or low a note sounds. C5 is the same note as C4, just higher.
card.codeText: "c4" is a value: a piece of data. Change the value and the sound changes.

listen.say: Listen. These notes go up, like walking up stairs!

melody.say: Drag the green melody block inside My song.
melody.hint: It's the green block with a gap inside.

notes.say: Put three notes inside the melody. Red C, then orange D, then yellow E.
notes.hint: Drag the red note in first. Then orange, then yellow underneath.

staff.say: Tap the Staff button to see your music written down!
staff.hint: The Staff button is at the top of the right side.

look.say: These five lines are called a staff. Higher notes sit higher on the staff. C sits on its own little line underneath!
look.hint: Look at the red, orange and yellow notes climbing.

play.say: Press Play and sing along: C, D, E!

card.musicText: Music is written on five lines called a staff. Higher notes sit higher up.
card.codeText: note() plays notes by name. c4 is the C in the middle of the piano.

listen.say: Listen. Some notes are long, and some are short.

notes.say: Make a melody with at least two notes.
notes.hint: Drag the melody block in, then put notes inside it.

half.say: Change one note to a half note. It lasts two beats. On the staff it has an empty, hollow head!
half.hint: Tap the word quarter on a note and choose half.

whole.say: Now try a whole note. It lasts four beats, and it has no stick!
whole.hint: Tap quarter or half on a note and choose whole.

fill.say: Fill one bar: make your notes add up to exactly four beats.
fill.hint: A whole note is 4 beats. A half note is 2. A quarter note is 1.

play.say: Press Play and count along: one, two, three, four!

code.say: In the code, the at sign makes a note longer. A bigger number means a longer note.
code.hint: The at signs are glowing yellow.

card.musicText: Whole = 4 beats. Half = 2 beats. Quarter = 1 beat. Eighth = half a beat.
card.codeText: In c4@2, the @ makes that note last twice as long as the others.

listen.say: Listen and count: one, two, three, four.

melody.say: Drag a melody block into My song.
melody.hint: The green block with a gap inside.

read1.say: Read the music in the box. Two quarter notes, then a half note. Can you build it?
read1.hint: Quarter notes have a filled head and a stick. A half note has a hollow head.

count.say: Look at your staff. Count it: one, two, three, four. The half note gets two counts!
count.hint: The half note is held for three and four.

read2.say: Read this one. The squiggly sign is a quarter rest. Be quiet for one beat!
read2.hint: Note, rest, note, note. Use the shh note for the rest.

code.say: In the code, the rest is a squiggle. Quiet for one step.

card.musicText: Rhythm is the pattern of long, short and silent beats. To read it, count the beats.
card.codeText: In note("e4 ~ e4 e4"), the ~ is a rest: one beat of silence.

listen.say: Listen. First the notes are short and bouncy. Then they are smooth and joined up.

notes.say: Make a melody with at least three notes.
notes.hint: Drag the melody block in, then add notes.

bouncy.say: Tap normal on your melody block and choose bouncy.
bouncy.hint: The word normal is next to melody.

dots.say: Look at the staff. Each note has a little dot. A dot means short and bouncy. Musicians call it staccato!
dots.hint: Look for dots under the notes.

slur.say: See the curved line over the notes? It's called a slur. It means smooth and joined up: legato!
slur.hint: The curve goes from the first note to the last.

play.say: Press Play and listen to your smooth tune.

card.musicText: Staccato notes are short and bouncy: a dot. Legato notes are smooth and joined: a curved slur.
card.codeText: .legato(0.3) makes each note short. .legato(1.5) makes notes overlap smoothly.

listen.say: Listen. A scale climbs up, step by step, like a ladder.

tune.say: Drag the ladder block, the scale tune, into My song.
tune.hint: The green block with a ladder.

build.say: Read the music. Build the whole ladder: steps 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8.
build.hint: Add eight steps. Change each number so they go up one at a time.

staff.say: Look at the staff. Each note sits one step higher: line, space, line, space!
staff.hint: Follow the notes up like stairs.

minor.say: Now change the ladder from happy to sad.

flats.say: Look! Some notes now have a flat sign. A flat makes a note a tiny bit lower.
flats.hint: The flat sign looks like a small b.

play.say: Press Play. Listen to your sad scale.

card.musicText: A scale is a ladder of notes going up step by step. Minor scales have flats.
card.codeText: n("0 1 2 3").scale("C4:minor"): the same step numbers, a different ladder.

chords.say: Drag the chords block into My song.
chords.hint: The purple block with chord names.

staff.say: Tap the Staff button to see your chords.
staff.hint: The Staff button is at the bottom.

snowman.say: On the staff, a chord's notes are stacked on top of each other, like a snowman!
snowman.hint: Each chord is three notes in one column.

read.say: Read the chord names in the box: C, A minor, F, G. Make your chords match!
read.hint: Tap each chord name on your block and change it.

play.say: Press Play. That's a famous chord pattern in lots of songs!

card.musicText: A chord is written as notes stacked up. The C chord is C, E and G.
card.codeText: Brackets with commas: notes that play at the same time.

listen.say: Listen. The same tune sounds happy, then sad!

tune.say: Drag the green ladder block, the scale tune, into My song.
tune.hint: It has a ladder at the front.

steps.say: Put three steps inside: step 1, step 3, and step 5.
steps.hint: Drag in a step and tap its number to change it.

play.say: Press Play. Does it sound happy?

sad.say: Tap the happy face and choose sad. Listen to the difference!
sad.hint: Tap the word happy on the ladder block.

code.say: The numbers are steps on a ladder. scale picks which ladder. Major sounds happy. Minor sounds sad.
code.hint: Look for scale and minor in the code.

card.musicText: Major scales sound bright and happy. Minor scales sound darker and sad.
card.codeText: n("0 2 4").scale("C4:minor") maps step numbers to real notes, like looking them up in a list.

listen.say: Listen. Three notes at the same time make a chord. Chords make music sound full and warm.

chords.say: Drag the rainbow chords block into My song.
chords.hint: The purple block with C, F, G, C on it.

play.say: Press Play. Those are four chords!

change.say: Tap one chord and change it to A minor. It sounds a little sad!
change.hint: Tap a chord name, then pick Am.

code.say: In the code, notes inside square brackets with commas play together. That's a chord!
code.hint: Look for the commas between notes.

drums.say: Add a beat block under your chords. Now you have a band!
drums.hint: Drag the purple beat block under the chords.

card.musicText: A chord is three or more notes played at the same time.
card.codeText: [c4,e4,g4]: square brackets group notes, and commas mean play them together.
